A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DynamicFormer study. All 28 pages of v1 and 21 pages of v2, including v2 Appendices A–F, support comparison of the text, equations, tables, and figures. Substantial reorganization does not prevent matching retained material.

before.justification: v1 reports original intersection-number prediction experiments, recursive-function activation comparisons, representation probes, and counterfactual interventions.

after.justification: v2 retains original prediction and interpretability experiments and reports additional baseline comparisons, genus-17 predictions, and linear-versus-nonlinear probing results.

M1.justification: The DRA formula, B/d Transformer branches, dynamic positional bias, PNA pooling, [DYN] tokens, Talking Modalities loss, and MAE objective remain unchanged. Much of v1 Section 5 moves to v2 Appendix C. Excluding the C tensor was already described in v1.

E1.justification: v2 extends intersection-number evaluation to genus 17, beyond v1's maximum evaluated genus 16. The underlying enumerative task and synthetic recursive function remain the same. Reallocating existing genera between training, ID, and OOD evaluation primarily changes the protocol.

E2.justification: v2 Figure 1 adds GLU, Swish, PolyNorm, and KAN to the recursive-function comparison. Its intersection-number comparisons add ReLU and separate Snake/DRA MLP baselines (Tables 2 and 4). Conversely, v1 Section 6.1's evaluated naive Inductive Conformal Prediction and Conformalized Quantile Regression comparisons disappear.

E3.justification: v1 inconsistently states training through genus 13 or 14 and labels genus 14 ID; v2 consistently states training through 13, ID evaluation across 1–13, and OOD evaluation across 14–17. The synthetic experiment changes from one 64-unit hidden layer to 64/32-unit layers and moves the training endpoint from 150 to 120. NCS reporting is dropped, and explicit linear/MLP probe comparisons are introduced. These are reported protocol revisions, without establishing which experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds an architecture comparison against MLPs and explicitly tests whether asymptotic parameters and subleading coefficients are recoverable linearly or nonlinearly. These substantially extend the architecture and representation analyses. The existing [DYN]/Talking Modalities ablation, Dilaton analysis, PCA, and causal interventions remain, sometimes in appendices.

E5.justification: v1's R² ± quantities disappear from the main prediction and ablation tables, and its explicit subleading-coefficient interval of ±531 is omitted. v2 instead tabulates conformal coverage and width by evaluation group, retaining the 90% target and probe uncertainty displays. Neither version specifies repeated-run or seed counts, so changed reporting does not establish changed replication.

E6.justification: The principal ID/OOD result tables are substantially replaced. v2 adds genus-17 results of R² 93.8, coverage 95.27, and CW 8.30, plus MLP comparisons and a linear subleading-coefficient probe result of R² 0.63 alongside the nonlinear 0.98 result. Activation-comparison and causal-table values also change. Revised or incompletely specified settings prevent interpreting these replacements as matched-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: The partition-function theorem, recursion, Dilaton identity, and asymptotic theorem remain, with background material partly moved to Appendix A. However, v2 omits v1 Section 3.1's explicit boundedness qualification required to keep infinite-dimensional sums finite, reducing the stated theoretical assumptions.

C1.justification: The central contributions—DynamicFormer, DRA, uncertainty estimation, and recovery of mathematical structure—remain. v2's abstract and conclusion refine the interpretability claim to nonlinear encoding of asymptotic parameters and polynomiality, and its abstract adds a broader novelty claim about modeling high-variance recursive functions with factorial growth.

C2.justification: v2 interprets probe comparisons as evidence of nonlinear representations and recasts B's weak prediction effect from unexpected to expected, citing its linear contribution. It removes v1's specific limitations concerning changed quantum Airy structures and inadequate conformal coverage. It also adds the simultaneous large-genus/large-marked-point regime as a future question.

D1.justification: v2 Appendix C adds a code-repository pointer, and Appendix E explicitly identifies conformal widths as logarithmic-scale quantities. Most architecture and input-encoding details are relocated rather than newly disclosed. Conversely, v1's explicit genus-15 setting for the causal analysis is no longer stated.

R1.justification: v2 adds targeted positioning against integer-sequence learning and time-series approaches, including Belcak et al., Ragni and Klein, and Miller et al., alongside KAN and emergent-world-representation references. Several generic Transformer, interpretability, and conformal references are removed. The overall positioning within AI for mathematics remains.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, methodological motivation, interpretability discussion, and conclusion are substantially rewritten. Related work becomes an introduction subsection, while mathematical background, data representation, architecture details, uncertainty estimation, and PCA are reorganized into Appendices A–F.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a different document layout and extensively restructures displays. The synthetic comparison expands from four to eight panels, probing expands from one to two heatmaps, ID/OOD tables become paired subtables, and prediction plots are consolidated into a three-row appendix figure. The architecture diagram and PCA plots move to appendices, and the causal table is transposed.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens empirical scrutiny through additional activation/KAN and MLP comparisons, explicit linear-versus-nonlinear probes, and a consistent genus-split description. These address weaknesses in assessing the architecture and representation claims. The gains are limited by removing R² uncertainty entries, calibration-baseline comparisons, and specific generalization and undercoverage limitations; the revision therefore supports a modest net improvement rather than a substantial one.
